Partner Integration Reference Version 2.2

Dailyhunt is offering it’s rich catalogue of content via a seamless API integration. This document describes the details on how a partner can integrate with its Content Syndication API. It will help you understand the technical details of how you can integrate with Dailyhunt’s API, expectations from you & the API protocol specification.

  • 22-May-2020 : [v2.2] Included shortned shareInfo and shareUrl for each item in items API

Getting Started

This section describes the technical details of how to invoke Dailyhunt’s Syndication API. It will help you understand how to use the API security, message signing & the API protocol needed for integration.



During onboarding, Dailyhunt will provision the following items for your integration:

Item Description
API Key API access key needed for authentication of the API client
Secret Key Needed for signing the API parameters to generate a signature for API authentication
Partner Code Partner identification code

You will need to include the following items in all the API calls:
Item Description
Unique Partner user id (puid) Your unique user id accessing Dailyhunt API
API Key API access key needed for authentication of the api user
API Signature The API authentication signature generated using Secret Key
Partner Code Partner identification code
Dailyhunt Cookie (dhFeedV1) Dailyhunt generated cookie (as received from the very first API call) per user

The following section describes in detail, the steps needed for integration, including how to generate some of the above fields & how to include them in the API calls.

Integration Checklist

  • Get API Keys and partner code from Dailyhunt

  • Establish Signature generation for requests and get response from APIs

  • Puid generation: Unique id for each user to be passed for each request

  • Choose channels from Applicable options below and get configured from Dailyhunt - News Channels - Video Channels - DailyShare Channels - Location Channels

  • Include language onboarding for user to select content language (Recommended)

  • Integrate Tracking API

  • Place attribution request along with tracking

  • Share estimated volume and rollout plan with Dailyhunt

API Security

Since the APIs are protected, you will need to generate a message signature using the secret key as described below and pass it along with the API Key to all the API calls.

API Key & Secret Key

  1. Dailyhunt will share the API Key & Secret Key with you through email.
  2. You will pass the API key on every API call.
  3. You will use the Secret Key for signing API requests & generate a Signature Base String that needs to be passed on every API call.

How to generate Signature Base String

To generate a Signature Base String, you will need to do the following steps:

  1. Append ts= in the url as query parameter.

  2. URL encode the parameter key & value pairs.

  3. Sort all the request query parameters lexicographically, sorted on encoded key.

  4. Append all the key=value with “_&_” as separator if more than one key=value is present.

  5. Uppercase the http method used in the url and in that, append the string from #4 above. This new string (encoded sorted parameters + uppercase http method) represents the Signature Base String.

For testing out the APIs in Postman, this collection includes a Pre-request Script, which handles the generation of Signature. You can use the test environment provided with the collection

Replace the below values by values provided by Dailyhunt to test, in the postman environment or the below sample snippets.

  • PARTNER_CODE
  • YOUR_API_KEY
  • YOUR_SECRET_KEY

Or use one of the below sample snippets which use API Key & Secret Key to generate signature and to invoke Dailyhunt API

import java.io.BufferedWriter;
import java.io.FileWriter;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.UnsupportedEncodingException;
import java.net.URLEncoder;
import java.security.InvalidKeyException;
import java.security.NoSuchAlgorithmException;
import java.security.SignatureException;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeMap;

import javax.crypto.Mac;
import javax.crypto.spec.SecretKeySpec;

import org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64;
import org.apache.http.HttpEntity;
import org.apache.http.client.methods.CloseableHttpResponse;
import org.apache.http.client.methods.HttpGet;
import org.apache.http.impl.client.CloseableHttpClient;
import org.apache.http.impl.client.HttpClients;
import org.apache.http.util.EntityUtils;
import org.json.simple.JSONObject;
import org.json.simple.parser.JSONParser;

public class APIClient {

  private static String PARTNER_CODE = "<PARTNER_CODE>";
  private static String API_KEY_VALUE = "<YOUR_API_KEY>";
  private static String SECRET_KEY = "<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>";
  private static String HTTP_METHOD_GET = "GET";
  
  public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
    APIClient client = new APIClient();
    
    // In query parameter always add the "ts" query parameter
    String queryParameter = "&langCode=en&partner="+PARTNER_CODE+"&cid=1&puid=test123&ts=" +
        System.currentTimeMillis();
    
    // Generate the signature base string
    String signatureBase = client.generateSignatureBase(HTTP_METHOD_GET, queryParameter);

    // Generate the signature i.e. Message Authentication Code using HMAC
    String signature = client.calculateRFC2104HMAC(signatureBase, SECRET_KEY);
    System.out.println("signature = " + signature);
    
    // Form the url & pass the API_KEY and the Signature generated in the header
    String httpUrl = "http://feed.dailyhunt.in/api/v2/syndication/items?" + queryParameter;
    Map<String, String> headers = new HashMap<>();
    headers.put("Authorization", "key=" + API_KEY_VALUE);
    headers.put("Signature", signature);
    
    // Now call the url now
    client.httpGet(httpUrl, headers,args[0]);
  }

  private String calculateRFC2104HMAC(String data, String key) throws SignatureException {
    String result;
    try {
      // get an hmac_sha1 key from the raw key bytes
      SecretKeySpec signingKey = new SecretKeySpec(key.getBytes(), "HmacSHA1");
      
      // get an hmac_sha1 Mac instance and initialize with the signing key
      Mac mac = Mac.getInstance("HmacSHA1");
      mac.init(signingKey);
      
      // compute the hmac on input data bytes
      byte[] rawHmac = mac.doFinal(data.getBytes());
      
      // base64-encode the hmac
      result = Base64.encodeBase64String(rawHmac);
    } catch (InvalidKeyException e) {
      throw new SignatureException("Failed to generate HMAC as key is invalid", e);
    } catch (NoSuchAlgorithmException e) {
      throw new SignatureException("Failed to generate HMAC as encoding algorithm does not exists", e);
    }
    return result;
  }
  
  private String generateSignatureBase(String httpMethod, String queryString) {
    StringBuilder signatureBaseBuffer = new StringBuilder();
    
    if (!isEmpty(queryString)) {
      Map<String, String> queryParams = urlRequestParamToMap(queryString);
      
      // Sort all the request query parameters lexicographically, sorted on encoded key
      Map<String, String> encodedAndSortedQueryParams = new TreeMap<>();
      for (String key : queryParams.keySet()) {
        encodedAndSortedQueryParams.put(urlEncodedString(key), 
            urlEncodedString(queryParams.get(key)));
      }
      
      // Append all the key=value with “&” as separator if more than one key=value is present
      signatureBaseBuffer.append(formatAsUrl(encodedAndSortedQueryParams));
    }
    // Append the UPPERCASE(http method)
    signatureBaseBuffer.append(httpMethod.toUpperCase());
    return signatureBaseBuffer.toString();
  }
  
  private boolean isEmpty(String str) {
    return null == str || (null != str && "".equals(str.trim()));
  }
  
  private Map<String, String> urlRequestParamToMap(String url) {
    if (isEmpty(url)) {
      return new HashMap<String, String>();
    }

    Map<String, String> keyValueMapping = new HashMap<>();
    String[] params = url.split("&");
    for (String param : params) {
      String[] keyValue = param.split("=");
      String key = keyValue[0];
      String value = keyValue.length == 2 ? keyValue[1] : "";
      keyValueMapping.put(key, value);
    }

    return keyValueMapping;
  }

  private String formatAsUrl(Map<String, String> pairs) {
    if (pairs == null) {
      return "";
    }

    StringBuilder urlBuilder = new StringBuilder();
    for (String key : pairs.keySet()) {
      if (urlBuilder.length() != 0) {
        urlBuilder.append("&");
      }
      urlBuilder.append(key).append("=").append(pairs.get(key));
    }

    return urlBuilder.toString();
  }
  
  private String urlEncodedString(String normalString) {
    try {
      return URLEncoder.encode(normalString, "UTF-8");
    } catch (UnsupportedEncodingException e) {
      return normalString;
    }
  }
  
  private void httpGet(String url, Map<String, String> headers,String fileName) throws IOException {
    CloseableHttpClient httpclient = HttpClients.createDefault();
    
    HttpGet httpGet = new HttpGet(url);
    for (String key : headers.keySet()) {
      httpGet.addHeader(key, headers.get(key));
    }
    
    CloseableHttpResponse response1 = httpclient.execute(httpGet);
    try {       
      try (FileWriter writer = new FileWriter(fileName);
          BufferedWriter bw = new BufferedWriter(writer)) {
        if(response1.getStatusLine().getStatusCode() == 200){
          HttpEntity entity1 = response1.getEntity();          
          String str = EntityUtils.toString(entity1, "UTF-8"); 
          JSONParser parser = new JSONParser();
          JSONObject json = (JSONObject) parser.parse(str);
          JSONObject data = (JSONObject)json.get("data");
          System.out.println(data.get("count"));
          Long c = (Long)data.get("count");
          bw.write(Long.toString(c));
        }else{
          bw.write(response1.getStatusLine().getStatusCode());
        }
      } catch (IOException e) {
          System.err.format("IOException: %s%n", e);
      }  
    }catch(Exception ex){
      System.out.println(ex);
    }finally {
        response1.close();
    }

  }
}

Passing API Key & Signature Request Headers

Following steps need to be followed to pass the API Key & Signature headers to Dailyhunt:

  1. You will pass the API key in the Authorization header with value as key=.
  2. You will generate a signature (Message Authentication Code - MAC) using the secure message Authentication code algorithm SHA1-HMAC as explained below: a. Generate a signature (S), S = SHA1-HMAC(Secret Key, Signature Base String). b. Base64 encode the signature (S), let's call it S64.
  3. While calling the API, include the signature (S) in the header as Signature:<value of S64 in 2.b above>
  4. If the API key & the signature are correct, Dailyhunt server will allow the API access, otherwise it will return error codes.

References

HMAC https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hash-based_message_authentication_code

Java HMAC https://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-codec/apidocs/org/apache/commons/codec/digest/HmacUtils.html

http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/AuthJavaSampleHMACSignature.html

Error Codes

You will get below error codes for failures:

401 If invalid API key is given in the request header
403 If invalid Signature is given in the request heade
500 For any unexpected issues at Dailyhunt

Example

curl -H"Authorization:key=<API Key>" -H"Signature:<value of S64>"" "http://<host:port>/api/v2/syndication/channels?partner=xxxx&puid=<your unique user id>&ts=<current server local timestamp>"

Handling CORS

Dailyhunt API can also be integrated directly from the browser. In order to avoid Cross-Origin issue, Dailyhunt supports Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS). Dailyhunt will provide the following headers in the preflight response with OPTIONS http method.

Access-Control-Allow-Origin:

Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true

For more information on CORS, you may refer https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-origin_resource_sharing

Identity Management

A unique user id is needed for every user accessing and consuming Dailyhunt’s content. Dailyhunt uses the user id to understand the user’s content consumption pattern and to serve personalized content to the user.

Following sections describe how you can pass a unique user id and the need for a Dailyhunt Cookie which needs to be maintained at your end.

Unique User ID

  1. You will need to provide a unique user id as query parameter in the Dailyhunt API calls. This could be any identifier such as a device identifier, if accessible and available.

Parameter Name: test123

Example: http://host:port/{{api_url}}?puid={{Your_unique_user_id}}

  1. Dailyhunt will generate & maintain an internal (Dailyhunt side) user id corresponding to your unique user id.

Dailyhunt Cookie

  1. When you access Dailyhunt API with your Unique User Id (i.e. “_puid_”) in the query parameter, Dailyhunt API will provide a user specific Cookie (dhFeedV1) in the API response.

  2. You are expected to maintain the dhFeedV1 Cookie per user at your end and pass it back on subsequent Dailyhunt API calls. For common browser based integrations, this should happen seamlessly.

  3. Dailyhunt will take care of (re-)generating the dhFeedV1 Cookie, if found missing in the request or if the Cookie is expired. Dailyhunt will reject the request if _dhFeedV1 _Cookie is found invalid.

  4. Dailyhunt Cookie helps avoid repeated lookup of the Dailyhunt internal user id for a given partner user id (puid) in every API call.

  5. Dailyhunt Cookie will be having a TTL of one month initially (and this may change in future).

Image Resolutions

Handling Image Url for Different Resolutions/Quality

The content fetch API provides images field, having one or more image urls for the story card. The image url will have the following format:

[http://bcdn.newshunt.com/{CMD}/{W}x{H}_{Q}/(image_folder).{EXT}]

Where,

  • {CMD} = one of “crop” or “resize” If cropped, Dailyhunt will return the exact image size center cropped If resized, Dailyhunt will return the size closest to the one specified.

  • {W} = Desired width of the image based on your user’s device dimension

  • {H} = Desired height of the image based on your user’s device dimension

  • {Q} = Desired image quality in percentage based on user’s network quality, highest possible value is 100 and quality value is directly proportional to the image file size

  • {EXT} = Desired image extension such as webp, jpg, etc.

You should take care of replacing the above placeholders with appropriate values matching your user’s device & network speed qualifier.

Dailyhunt will dynamically generate each image matching your criteria & cache on Dailyhunt’s CDN.

Feature Mask for advanced features

The pfm(Partner feature mask) parameter in Channels and Items API controls which features are enabled for a particular partner or channel. In basic integration, only news items are served under each channel. For advanced cards and features like videos and DailyShare cards etc, the appropriate value of pfm has to be set.

The value of pfm is the sum of all bit vlaues of desired features by a partner.

Each feature is controlled by a specific bit defined.

List of available features:

Feature Value
LIVE_TV_CARD 1
CRICKET_CARD(Brief) 8
HERO_CARD 16
VIDEO_CHANNELS 32
VIRAL_CHANNELS 64

*Bit 2 and 4 are reserved for some default feature.

For example:

If a partner wants to get HERO cards and Videos, the pfm value needs to be set to 16+32 = 48

Ideally, the pfm should be set at the channels API level. The contenUrl of each channel in the response inherently has the desired value of fm.

The value of fm of a particular channel should only be modified in case there is specific change needed in one particular channel.

Managing Clickouts

  • When your user clicks on a story card, you will invoke the story card deepLinkUrl which is given in the syndication/items api response

    You need to add the below to deepLinkUrl:

    • Unique puid
    • Dailyhunt Cookie (dhFeedV1) while calling deepLinkUrl

    For e.g:

    If the deepLinkUrl received from the items API is:

    http://m.dailyhunt.in/news/india/english/ibtimes-epaper-ibtimes/just+let+the+original+be+malaika+arora+on+chaiyya+chaiyya+being+recreated-newsid-168150810?mode=pwa&s=&ss=Browser-Feed&utm_source=&utm_medium=Browser-Feed&utm_campaign=-Browser-Feed&lite=true&prevRef=1&partnerRef=%7B%22pid%22%3A%22%22%7D

    append puid

    http://m.dailyhunt.in/news/india/english/ibtimes-epaper-ibtimes/just+let+the+original+be+malaika+arora+on+chaiyya+chaiyya+being+recreated-newsid-168150810?mode=pwa&s=&ss=Browser-Feed&utm_source=&utm_medium=Browser-Feed&utm_campaign=-Browser-Feed&lite=true&prevRef=1&partnerRef=%7B%22pid%22%3A%22%22%7D**&puid={puid_value}**

  • Dailyhunt will include the some explicit tracking parameters in the deepLinkUrl. These parameters should be retained as is.

For eg: s, ss, utm_medium, partnerRef etc.

These are important to ensure proper tracking and attribution.

The deep link URL will either open in the browser (if user does not have Dailyhunt app installed) or in the Dailyhunt app (if user has Dailyhunt app installed & chooses to open with Dailyhunt app)

Managing Tracking

To help measure/track the cards seen by the user, you will need to pass the tracking data for each item card seen by your user. To enable this, Dailyhunt provides the tracking data & tracking POST URLs in the Content Fetch API response.

This tracking needs to be enabled for each list view. A call is required to be made to dailyhunt tracking server for every list view that is invoked:

  • As the first page in a new channel
  • As the next page in the same channel
  • On load of the list

How to track the seen cards

  1. Dailyhunt provides trackData field for each card, this is mentioned in the Content Fetch API section,
  2. In the same response above, Dailyhunt also provides a tracking POST URL via the trackUrl field.

You will need to form an array of the trackData values and POST the same to the trackUrl for the cards seen by the user. For e.g, if the pageSize is 10, the track request will contain 10 items in the array.

You can do this periodically or every time user sees a page worth of cards (as close to the user activity as possible). Please refer to Tracking API for more details.

Attribution

ComScore is a provider for audience measurement using Unified Digital Measurement® (UDM) methodology, which accounts for all unique site visitors from all platforms. It is an industry standard traffic attribution tool that helps advertisers validate attributable traffic data to each site / app / service etc.

For each Pageview that occurs on a particular URL, a single ping is sent to ComScore to count the respective pageview as valid. You can find more info here - https://www.comscore.com/About

Comscore ListView attribution

The requirement is that the partner places this tracking pixel on the list page so that all list pageviews that occur can be attributed as Dailyhunt content pageviews on ComScore. When each page is loaded (page 1, page 2 etc.), this ping will need to be made.

A call is required to be made to comscore for every list view that is invoked:

  • As the first page in a new channel
  • As the next page in the same channel
  • On load of the list

This can be done alongside each tracking call for list views.

How to get the ComScore Url?

The ComscoreUrl that needs to be pinged is available as a part of Content Fetch API , as shown below:

 "track": {
        "comscoreUrls": [
            "http://b.scorecardresearch.com/p?c1=2&c2=21733245&c4=http://m.dailyhunt.in/news/&c9=m.dailyhunt.in"
        ]
    }

There are two options to do this basis the protocol used HTTP or HTTPS .

  1. Via javascript placed within the page (for browser integrations)
  2. Direct call (for native or any other non-browser integrations)

Javascript Approach

Include the below script tag for every list view:

<div id="csDiv"></div> <script> document.getElementById("csDiv").innerHTML = '<img src="PLACE COMSCORE URL DYNAMICALLY FROM THE API HERE" />'; </script>

Direct URL Approach

In this approach the client loading content page needs to fire a call to ComScore url fetched from the API.

This calls sets cookie back to client on 1st time call. Client needs to pass this cookie in all subsequent calls to ComScore. All standard libraries handles it automatically.

Collecting User Feedback On Cards

For all the cards displayed at your end, your user may want to give feedback about the cards seen. Dailyhunt provides ability to show the specific feedback options that can be displayed to your user & allow to send the signals to the Dailyhunt server. Dailyhunt will use these signals to further improve the personalized feed of your user. Refer : Feedback API

Image height and width is returned as a part of the response. To handle the UI for cards/images received from Dailyshare, Dailyhunt recommends below aspect ratios:

width = height 1:1
width > height 16:9 , 4:3
height > width 1:1 (center crop)

Live Cricket Feed Integration

Dailyhunt exposes cricket matches feed through APIs and the same can be used for integration in your app.

Cricket Channel

Dailyhunt provides Cricket channel that will provide a list of the upcoming, current & past matches. The below table describes the channel fields and descriptions of a Cricket Channel.

Channel Field Cricket Channel Description Data Type
id The cricket channel id String
type The channel type will be CRICKET String
name The channel name will be Cricket in unicode String
contentUrl The cricket matches browse API url as explained below String
deepLinkUrl This is not used currently

Browse Cricket Matches

Like every other channel, Cricket channel also will have a content fetch API that is of the form /syndication/items. The cricket channel content Fetch API provides a way to dynamically explore the list of upcoming, current & past cricket matches.

Below table describes the fields of a Cricket Match that will be given in the /syndication/items API response.

Item Field Cricket Match Description Data Type
id The cricket match id String
type The item type will be “CRICKET” String
title The title of the cricket match String
matchDate* The start date time of the cricket match Long
team1* The cricket match playing first team Team Object
team2* The cricket match playing second team Team Object
streamUrl* The score streaming api url of the cricket match String
commentaryUrl* The commentary streaming api url of the cricket match as described in section “Stream Cricket Match Commentary API” String
trackData The tracking data for the match String
trackFrequency* The time gap in milliseconds for POSTing trackData to Dailyhunt Long

* - fields specific to "Cricket Match" item (not applicable to other content types)

The fields of the "Team" object above has the following attributes:

Field Description Data Type
id The team id of the cricket match String
teamName The short name of the team such as IND, AUS etc String
teamIcon The flag image url of the team String

Tracking Cricket Match

A match card in the Browse Cricket section has the trackData attribute and you can use the same tracking approach mentioned in the section - Managing Tracking to POST the cricket score views to Dailyhunt. Just that, the frequency of POSTing the trackData for cricket content refreshes, will be managed by the trackFrequency field given along with the trackData.
